subject: Problems trying to estimate DSM variance

messages.author: 232ea38fda21e4b9
messages.subject: Problems trying to estimate DSM variance
parts:
Hello All,

I have been trying to estimate the variance of my DSM. I initially started this DSM analysis last year and am using the older version of the dolphin code. 

var.nb390k <- dsm.var.prop(dam_AD_ESA_GAM_NB390K, predgrid, off.set=predgrid$off.set, seglen.varname="Effort", type.pred="response")

I keep getting the following error,

Error:cannot allocate vector of size 305.4Mb
In addition:Warning messages:
1: In `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`,  "off.set", value = c(0,0,0,0,0, :
Reached total allocation of 16292Mb: see help(memory.size)

I have increased my memory limit using memory.limit(size=) but I still get these errors (but with larger numbers like 32 GB).

The size of my predgrid is large because I am using 6 30m-resolution raster layers covering a large area. How can I work around the memory issue?

Thank you for any and all help!

Sarah

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Problems trying to estimate DSM variance
parts:
Hi Sarah, hi listfolk,

This is a tricky issue and one I've been battling myself in some
modelling I've been doing. If you only require a map of the uncertainty
from the variance procedure, then you can split up the grid into bits,
get the per-cell uncertainties and then put the data back together at
the end to make your plot etc.

If you need a total variance/CV/etc at the end, things are a bit more
tricky. Drop me an e-mail, we can discuss more off-list and post our
solution back here once we get somewhere.

cheers,
--dave
